2610.13810.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
2610.13810.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are now a standard source of query expansion terms but they hallucinate. They inject non existent entities and off-topic terms that add ranking noise and can hurt strong retrievers. Existing remedies such as corpus grounding, mutual verification and preference alignment treat hallucinated terms as an undifferentiated nuisance to be filtered by agreement heuristics, without a mechanistic account of why a given term appears or a principled criterion for how many terms to keep. We propose Subsequence-Association Filtered, breadth-aware query expansion (SAFE-QE), a training-free, retriever agnostic method that draws on the subsequence-association account of hallucination. We score each candidate expansion term by its corpus conditioned cross-context reproducibility, terms that reappear under randomised query contexts yet lack support in the pseudo-relevant set are flagged as products of dominant hallucinatory associations and down-weighted. Drawing on the characterisation of language generation as a trade-off between consistency (no hallucination) and breadth (coverage), we cast term selection as constrained coverage maximisation over the pseudo-relevant set, keeping a set that is approximately broad but consistent and stable across resampling. We also introduce the Hallucinated Expansion Term Rate, a query side faithfulness metric that counts injected expansion terms no relevant document supports. We evaluate our approach on benchmarked TREC and BEIR collections. Our SAFE-QE is statistically indistinguishable from generative and corpus-steered expansion on nDCG@10 while injecting fewer unsupported terms 4.3 per query against 27.8 for Query2doc and 57.5 for HyDE and on a strong learned sparse retriever, where every expansion method regresses. Faithfulness is therefore available at no measurable cost in ranking quality.
2610.13810.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）現在是查詢擴展術語的標準來源，但它們會產生幻覺。<lb/>它們注入不存在的實體和不相關的術語，這會增加排名噪聲並可能損害強大的檢索器。<lb/>現有的補救措施，如語料庫基礎、相互驗證和偏好對齊，將幻覺術語視為需要通過一致性啟發式過濾的無差別干擾，而沒有對為何某個術語出現的機制性解釋或對保留多少術語的原則性標準。<lb/>我們提出了子序列關聯過濾的、具廣度意識的查詢擴展（SAFE-QE），這是一種無需訓練、與檢索器無關的方法，基於幻覺的子序列關聯解釋。<lb/>我們通過其在語料庫條件下的跨上下文重現性來評分每個候選擴展術語，那些在隨機查詢上下文中重新出現但在偽相關集內缺乏支持的術語被標記為主導幻覺關聯的產物並降低權重。<lb/>基於將語言生成特徵化為一致性（無幻覺）和廣度（覆蓋範圍）之間的權衡，我們將術語選擇視為對偽相關集的約束性覆蓋最大化，保持一個大致廣泛但在重抽樣中一致且穩定的集合。<lb/>我們還引入了幻覺擴展術語率，這是一個查詢端的忠實度指標，用於計算沒有相關文檔支持的注入擴展術語。<lb/>我們在基準的 TREC 和 BEIR 集合上評估我們的方法。<lb/>我們的 SAFE-QE 在 nDCG@10 上與生成和語料庫驅動的擴展在統計上無法區分，同時每次查詢注入的無支持術語數量為 4.3，而 Query2doc 為 27.8，HyDE 為 57.5，並且在一個強大的學習稀疏檢索器上，每種擴展方法都會回退。因此，忠實度在排名質量上沒有可測量的成本。
